R-3.claim: gate leg: every registered C2/OPEN-3 carrier is consistent -- it is an owner ruling item that does not block sign-off, and the implementer did not self-rule

R-4.claim: additivity: the C1/OPEN-3 text corrections landed append-only (pre-change bytes survive as prefixes)
R-4.shape_note: handoff.json is JSON; byte-append is not its coherence criterion. R-3 covers its registration instead.

why_four_legs_and_not_fewer: R-1 alone would let a contradiction survive (presence without absence). R-2 alone would let a deletion masquerade as a resolution (absence without presence). R-3 is a distinct claim: the gate's registered STATUS is coherent and the implementer did not self-rule. R-4 is again distinct: it asks not 'is the right text there' but 'did it get there without destroying earlier bytes'. Four separable claims, four separable failure modes.

error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.error: path-depth off-by-one: REPO = EXEC.parents[6] resolved to <audit dir>, not the repo root (correct is EXEC.parents[4])
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.how_caught: the path-sanity guard (git rev-parse --show-toplevel must equal REPO) reported FATAL: REPO != git toplevel
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.why_it_matters: without the guard, `git show HEAD:<wrong path>` returns EMPTY stdout, and the emptiness is then misreported as a CONTENT DEFECT -- the T1-13 failure mode. This is the SECOND time this same root cause has been hit in this batch (T1-13 was the first), and the guard converted it from a silent false positive into an explicit fatal.
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.lesson: a guard is valuable not because it prevents mistakes but because it makes them surface as FATAL rather than as FALSE REPORT
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.fixed_in: scripts/verify_t17.py (depth comment written from EXEC, not from __file__)

error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.error: anchor criterion compared incompatible hash functions: `git hash-object` returns a git BLOB hash (SHA-1 over 'blob <len>\0' + content) while the registered anchor is a SHA-256 of the on-disk bytes
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.symptom: [anchor] FAIL with 20bca1626a015ce3... while sha256sum still read 9ec65295...
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.how_caught: the reported value did not match the anchor, and the anchor had been independently reconfirmed as 9ec65295... via sha256sum
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.fixed_by: hashing the file with the same function the anchor was made with: hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes())
error_made_and_corrected_in_this_card.lesson: a criterion must match not only the object's FORM but the TYPE of the quantities being compared; two things both called 'hash' can be incomparable
